tagline: Leading the world in athletic footwear, apparel and equipment innovation.
hero_kpi_rationale: NIKE is the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel globally. Its overall performance is directly tied to total revenues, which reflect consumer demand and the effectiveness of its commercial strategy.

kpis.name: Revenues
kpis.explanation: Total amount of sales from athletic footwear, apparel, equipment and services.
kpis.description: Revenues declined by 10% for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, reflecting strategic adjustments in the market.
kpis.signal: Revenue decline, impacted by inventory management and repositioning strategy.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenues remaining after deducting cost of sales.
kpis.description: Gross margin decreased to 42.7% for fiscal 2025, compared to 44.6% the prior year.
kpis.signal: Declining gross margin, potentially impacted by new customs regulations and inventory clearance actions.

kpis.name: EBIT Margin
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest and taxes as a percentage of revenues.
kpis.description: EBIT margin dropped to 8.2% for fiscal 2025, down from 12.7% the previous year.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in operating margin, reflecting pressure on revenues and expenses.

kpis.name: ROIC
kpis.explanation: Performance metric that evaluates the company's ability to generate returns on invested capital after taxes.
kpis.description: ROIC declined to 20.2% for the four quarters ended May 31, 2025, from 34.9% the prior year.
kpis.signal: Significant decrease in return on invested capital.

kpis.name: Footwear Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of athletic footwear, a major segment representing approximately 64% of NIKE Brand revenues.
kpis.description: Footwear revenues decreased by 12% for fiscal 2025.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in footwear sales, the company's core segment.

kpis.name: Apparel Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the sale of athletic apparel, representing approximately 29% of NIKE Brand revenues.
kpis.description: Apparel revenues decreased by 6% for fiscal 2025.
kpis.signal: Decline in apparel sales, less pronounced than footwear.

kpis.name: NIKE Direct Sales
kpis.explanation: Revenue from NIKE-owned stores and digital platforms, representing approximately 42% of NIKE Brand revenues.
kpis.description: Sales through NIKE Direct declined by 13% for fiscal 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant decline in direct sales, indicating challenges in retail and digital commerce.

kpis.name: Wholesale Sales
kpis.explanation: Revenue from sales to independent distributors, licensees and sales representatives, representing approximately 58% of NIKE Brand revenues.
kpis.description: Wholesale sales decreased by 7% for fiscal 2025.
kpis.signal: Decline in wholesale sales, less pronounced than direct sales.

kpis.name: EBIT
kpis.explanation: Operating profit before deduction of interest expenses and income taxes.
kpis.description: EBIT decreased by 42% to reach $3.778 billion for fiscal 2025.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Total profit after all expenses, including taxes and interest, representing net income attributable to shareholders.
kpis.description: Net income fell by 44% for fiscal 2025, amounting to $3.219 billion.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in net income, reflecting operational performance.

kpis.name: Currency-neutral revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenue measure that excludes the impact of foreign exchange rate fluctuations to better reflect underlying business trends.
kpis.description: Currency-neutral revenues declined by 9% for fiscal 2025, indicating intrinsic weakness in demand.
kpis.signal: Revenue performance, adjusted for currency effects, remains negative.

kpis.name: Demand creation expense
kpis.explanation: Investments in marketing and advertising to stimulate consumer demand, including brand marketing and sports marketing.
kpis.description: Demand creation expenses increased by 9% for fiscal 2025, reaching $4.689 billion, to support product launches and key sports moments.
kpis.signal: Increase in marketing expenses despite declining revenues.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale.

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury).
kpis.description: Cumulative dividends + share buybacks (2021-2025) in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée. >80 % = potentiellement non soutenable.

risks.title: Decline in revenues and profitability
risks.score_rationale: The 10-K indicates a significant decline in revenues (-10%) and profitability (EBIT -42%) in 2025 compared to 2024. This negative trend is explicitly mentioned in the 'RESULTS OF OPERATIONS' section and directly impacts financial performance. Revenues decreased from $51.362B to $46.309B.

risks.title: Decline in digital and direct sales
risks.score_rationale: NIKE Direct sales declined by 13% (fiscal 2025: $18.783B vs $21.519B), with a pronounced drop in digital sales linked to repositioning strategies. This is detailed in the 'NIKE BRAND REVENUE HIGHLIGHTS' section and represents a strategically important sales channel.

risks.title: Pricing pressure and impact on gross margins
risks.score_rationale: The MD&A explicitly states: 'As a result of the new tariffs, we expect to incur a material gross incremental increase to Cost of sales' and 'for fiscal 2026, we expect a negative impact on gross margin.' Gross margin declined from 44.6% to 42.7% in FY2025.

ai_positioning.summary: The company NKE does not mention artificial intelligence (AI) or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
